comparator.name: Medicine (Geneeskunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The Compas example for September 2026 entrants includes 60 EC in each year. The major includes 156 EC, with a 6 EC bachelor thesis. The first-listed 24 EC faculty minor is Amsterdam Global Health, subject to selection, capacity and future offering. The extra thesis in the 30 EC version for visiting students does not enter the ledger. Year two requires the binding study advice threshold of 42 first-year EC. Year three requires all of year one and 30 EC in year two. Minor entry additionally requires 18 EC from semester 2.1. The care placement requires preparation or equivalent skills accepted by its examiner. GP placement requires satisfactory professional behavior in the care placement and examiner approval. Patient-related teaching requires confidentiality and participation. The Dutch language test or remedial work gates Doctor and Patient 1. Clinical, progress and portfolio assessments and research introductions are embedded. The bachelor thesis normally follows the minor and uses a short systematic review or an eligible report of research-minor work. It is supervised and written individually in scientific English. The current registration deadlines apply to the current third-year cohort. VUMED360 starts in September 2027. Compas regular teaching ends after 2028–2029, and the last graduation date is 31 August 2030. Compas credits do not transfer into VUMED360.
components: A supervised placement in a care setting. Students must complete the preparatory practicals or demonstrate equivalent skills.
Includes the general practice placement. Students need satisfactory professional behavior in the care placement and examiner approval.
An example faculty minor on primary and community care, health inequalities and diversity. Admission and availability apply.
An individually supervised thesis in scientific English. Students write a short systematic review or, after an eligible research minor, report their own research.

core: Human body, biological disease mechanisms and treatment science
Psychological functioning, development and the person experiencing illness
Medical scientific research and critical evaluation
Humane medicine, population health and diversity in society

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: introduces research design, sampling and inferential tests before advanced medical evidence evaluation
studies legal rights, liberty and equality and their enforcement as the rights framework for humane treatment of diverse populations; it is not a specialist health-law course

Studies virtue, deontological and consequentialist ethical reasoning, moral responsibility and practical ethical argument; a normative complement to humane medicine, not a specialist medical-ethics or clinical decision-making course.
studies race, gender, institutions and social interaction as the social-diversity dimension explicitly requested by this Medicine target

Develops qualitative design, data collection, interpretation and reflexivity in a group research project; supports investigation of social experience and participatory community health, not clinical history-taking.
studies solidarity, social trust and migrant inclusion with a civil-society organisation project, implementing the evidenced social-diversity direction rather than a clinical substitute
studies disease risks, screening, prevention and epidemiological evidence for population-health decisions
develops structure-function reasoning across body systems using imaging and anatomical materials; these are academic experiences, not clinical skills training
explains drug targets, pharmacokinetics and pharmacological models connecting treatment to molecular and physiological mechanisms
studies host-pathogen interaction, immunity and inflammatory disease
connects anatomy and physiology with symptoms and pathophysiology in six organ systems

Studies evolutionary and comparative animal neurobiology, biorhythms, disorders, animal models and research ethics, with basic microscopy/cell-staining work; a specific neuroscience complement, not a human neurological examination course.
develops the cognitive-neuroscience account of advanced mental functions relevant to the external cognition and neuropsychological strand
establishes cellular and organismal biology needed for the anatomy, physiology and disease-mechanism sequence
introduces functional brain anatomy, psychological theories and clinical-psychology methods before advanced human-behaviour study
studies cellular signalling, gene regulation, cell fate and drug mechanisms underlying normal function and disease
studies adult organ-system function, homeostasis and integrated physiology; it expressly does not claim full medical physiology
explains biomolecules, metabolism and molecular failures associated with disease
practises blood analysis, bacterial identification, protein and DNA laboratory methods used in biological and clinical research
studies cell injury, inflammation, neoplasia, genetic disease, testing and treatment
studies social influences on feelings, beliefs and behaviour relevant to health behaviour and the person behind the patient

Applies multivariate statistical models including linear/logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of (co)variance and nonparametric tests to human-science data; supports medical evidence analysis without reproducing the whole medical research unit.
studies mental disorders, classification, assessment and treatment through a biopsychosocial framework
examines health behaviour, stress, chronic illness experience and psychological interventions in medical settings
studies psychological assessment, psychodiagnostics, psychotherapy and their ethical limits; it does not provide physician training
conducts systematic reviews and meta-analysis in R to evaluate treatment evidence
studies prenatal through late-life physical, cognitive, emotional and social development relevant to development and illness across the lifespan

alternatives.label: Biomedicine, neuroscience & health psychology
alternatives.concept: Study how the human body functions, how disease develops and how medicines act. Connect laboratory work and research methods with the study of the brain, mental health and the experience of illness.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has substantial biomedical, cognitive and clinical-psychology sequences; the label avoids suggesting a full Medicine curriculum.
progression: Biology and behavior foundations precede organ-system physiology, pharmacology and advanced psychology. Research design precedes statistics and evidence synthesis.

alternatives.label: Biomedicine, population health & social inclusion
alternatives.concept: Study human function and disease alongside the social factors that shape health. Use epidemiology, qualitative research and social psychology to investigate who faces health risks and how communities respond.
alternatives.labelReason: Biomedicine remains the foundation, while social psychology, qualitative research, civil-society inquiry and rights replace four neurocognitive/therapeutic courses. The social-inclusion emphasis is bounded by actual general social-course content, not a claim to public-health professional preparation.
progression: Biomedical and social foundations precede disease mechanisms, health psychology and social inquiry. Epidemiology, qualitative methods and evidence synthesis examine population and community health.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each programme: neurobiology, higher cognitive functions, psychodiagnostics/psychotherapies and lifespan psychology are replaced by social psychology, qualitative research, contemporary social theory and human rights. These changes implement the social-inclusion concept rather than arbitrary breadth.

candidates.label: Learning medicine through supervised patient contact

selection.assessment: Two distinct qualified responses are supported by the verified biomedical/psychological core and the exact-target diversity/population-health direction, including the selected minor’s social determinants and community-research content. The second changes four courses/30 EC toward social psychology, qualitative methods, civil society and rights. Supervised patient-contact learning cannot be supplied by academic anatomy, laboratory cases or psychodiagnostics; that candidate remains not feasible. No third programme is manufactured from postgraduate careers or illustrative activities.

blocks: Both study how body structure supports function. VU also teaches musculoskeletal examination and clinical reasoning.
Both study infection, inflammation and immune defenses. VU also studies clinical presentation and treatment across infectious and inflammatory conditions.
Both study cardiovascular disease mechanisms. UCR compares cases across several organ systems, while VU develops cardiovascular diagnosis and treatment in more depth.
Both study how the body regulates its internal environment. UCR surveys normal organ-system function, while VU connects regulation to clinical problems.
Both study nutrient metabolism and biochemical regulation. VU integrates metabolism with anatomy, physiology and clinical examination.
Both study cell injury, inflammation and tissue repair. UCR also studies genetic mechanisms of disease.
VU integrates anatomical foundations with the study of organs and clinical skills.
VU studies circulation, fluid balance and related medical problems in a dedicated course.
VU studies the beginning of life in a dedicated medical course.
VU studies blood disorders and cancer in a dedicated medical course. UCR studies related cellular and genetic mechanisms.
VU develops clinical reasoning about digestive and metabolic disorders. UCR studies underlying function and disease mechanisms across courses.
Both examine the structure and function of the nervous system. VU develops sensory pathways, neurological lesions and sensory examinations in more depth.
Both examine mental disorders, their assessment and treatment. UCR approaches these questions through academic psychology, while VU also develops psychiatric examination.
Both examine health behavior, lifestyle and chronic illness. UCR emphasizes psychological and social influences on health, while VU also studies prevention and health services.
Both examine how people develop physically and psychologically. UCR covers the whole lifespan, while VU focuses on pediatric growth and clinical problems.
VU studies sex, sexuality and relationships in a medical context.
VU develops clinical reasoning in neurology and ophthalmology. UCR studies related aspects of brain function and disease.
Both teach empirical study design and statistical analysis. VU applies these methods to medical research questions.
Both use regression and statistical analysis to answer research questions. VU also develops epidemiology and other methods in a medical context.
VU requires a 6 EC individual medical thesis. UCR teaches evidence synthesis in a course. Its optional independent research sits outside the displayed schedules.
Population health, social inclusion and clinical formation
The first Doctor and Patient course introduces medical skills, communication and professional development.
The second Doctor and Patient course continues medical skills and introduces research practice.
VU requires a supervised placement in a care setting.
The third Doctor and Patient course continues clinical skills and professional development.
The fourth Doctor and Patient course includes experience in general practice.
The fifth Doctor and Patient course integrates clinical skills and professional preparation for further medical study.
The VU minor brings together primary care, community health and diversity. The second UCR option addresses social influences on health across several courses.

notes.text: VU includes supervised patient contact, medical examinations and clinical reasoning throughout the degree. It requires placements in care and general practice. UCR studies related biomedical, psychological and population-health questions through coursework and academic research.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Medicine combines study of the human body and disease with clinical reasoning, patient communication, placements and medical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Both UCR options study human function and disease. One emphasizes neuroscience and health psychology. The other applies epidemiology and social inquiry to population health and inclusion.

curriculum.routeLabel: Compas curriculum; Amsterdam Global Health minor
curriculum.limitation: This 180 EC Compas example is for September 2026 entrants. It includes a 24 EC minor and a 6 EC thesis. Year three requires all first-year credits and 30 EC from year two, including at least 18 EC from semester 2.1 for the minor. Regular Compas teaching ends after 2028–2029, and the final graduation date is 31 August 2030.
